exposure: obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) care bundle
Women giving birth to neonates weighing 3500 g
Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. vacuum extraction)
Use of elements of an obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) care bundle (communication, visible perineum, hand on fetal head, perineal support, certification)
cohort: 10,383 women giving birth vaginally from gestational week 22 + 0
finding: Both the 'hand on the fetal head' and 'perineal support' elements of the OASI care bundle were independently associated with a reduced risk of OASI.
